newsitem.title: UK: Edinburgh says Q1 performance on track.
newsitem.headline: Edinburgh says Q1 performance on track.

text.p: Edinburgh Fund Managers Group Plc chairman Colin Ross said on Tuesday first quarter performance was in line with its profit expectations.

He told the group's annual general meeting investment performance in certain areas in the past had not been as he would have wished, but significant steps had been taken to improve the performance and the initial results from the implementation of its enhanced investment process were encouraging.
"The path is now clear for us to build the group into a major force in the fund management industry. This can only be achieved through consistent above average investment performance," Ross said.

EFM's funds under management will fall to 6.7 billion sterling at the end of April from 7.6 billion following the loss of much of the British Investment Trust (BIT) portfolio after a restructuring at BIT.

BIT said in March it had completed agreements which saw it selling its 32.5 percent stake in EFM in a restructuring following a decision by 84.9 percent shareholder the British Coal Pension Schemes that it was no longer appropriate for it to hold such a significant proportion of its assets in a quoted investment trust.
EFM raised pre-tax profits 41 percent to 18 million sterling before exceptionals in the year to January 31.

But Ross said BIT's subsequent liquidation had resulted in a wider and more stable shareholder base for EFM. Minority shareholders of BIT have become unit holders in Edinburgh Global Value Fund which began trading on Monday.
The fund's size was about 64 million sterling.

"The first quarter has progressed in line with our profit expectations. The future success of the Group is now dependent on our ability to provide clients with solid investment performance and products which meet their needs. I am confident that we can achieve this goal."
